answer: A landmark checkpoint ledger resists sybil attacks by tying each agent identity to a distinct sequence of physical check-ins at a local karst spring, with copied sequences rejected. To clone an identity, an attacker must reproduce separate real visits and pay the per-identity travel, time, and verification cost for each duplicate. Because every copy diverges at the next checkpoint, duplication becomes self-revealing, so a jade trader or mesa guide cannot silently reuse the same visit history.
